_help: Talking manual, step AM4-r5 (the review of ed813ab, MED-1 / MED-2): manual sentences that MUST be offerable to the
extract mode (answer.pick_units over the passage + its following passages of the same heading, index.following)
AND must carry their limiting sentence in the SAME unit. Each entry: lang, id = the passage id of the committed
index (groundstation/assistant/index/manual_<lang>.json), pick = a substring of the statement, must = a substring
of the limit (null = the statement itself is the point), more = true when the unit may be the cap fallback (the
statement + its FIRST limit, marked 'more limits - see the manual'). Test AS25 checks every entry on the real
index; a passage id moves when the manual changes - then fix the id here (the pick text finds it: the test
prints the passage that holds the pick text).
known_limits = statements that are NOT joined with a later sentence BY DESIGN (W126): the limit stands under
another heading (the chain stops at a heading) or the pick opens with a pronoun (LOW-2: never offered alone). The
test asserts these stay as documented.
never_alone (step AM4-r6, review of a8bb45f MED-2): statements whose EXCEPTION follows (an 'exception' / 'however' /
«Εξαίρεση» / «ωστόσο» sentence, or one opening with «Όμως» / 'But') are NEVER offered without it: joined within the
cap, or (statement + exception over 60 words) not offered at all - the exception sentence itself may stand alone.
Fields: lang, id, pick = a substring of the statement, limit = a substring of the exception sentence. Test AS25
asserts no offered unit holds pick without limit and that its own rule sees the exception as a limit (mutation:
without the exception words both statements are offered alone).
